Subject: Dedicated sizing — expected burst windows and ask for tranche proposal

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week. We're progressing internally and procurement asked me to get firm guidance on how Redwood would size Dedicated GPU capacity tied to our expected workload spikes. A few specifics:

- Primary model: polaris-7B-finetune, typical batch inference at 512 tokens.
- Baseline steady-state: ~120 concurrent sessions, ~6M tokens/day.
- Peak windows: two daily windows (09:00–11:00 and 18:00–20:00 PT) where throughput can jump 6–8x for short bursts (5–20 minutes).
- Requirement: <250ms tail latency for interactive use during peaks if possible; otherwise graceful degradation with documented fallback.

We'd like a tranche-based proposal: reserved baseline capacity + an agreed burst mechanism (credits or ephemeral pool) and a clear eviction/priority policy so our critical inference jobs are preserved. Also procurement needs a sample of how headroom credits are consumed across a month so they can budget.

Can you put together a short tranche sizing proposal and soft-eviction policy we can review? Attach any assumptions/worksheets.

Best,
Asha
Procurement, Polaris Bio

Subject: Fwd: Dedicated sizing — Polaris ask (draft tranche proposal)

Team — forwarding Polaris ask. Key asks: tight tail latency in peak windows, tranche/credits model, and visibility for procurement. I'm drafting a tiered tranche matrix but want ops/infra input on eviction ordering and preemptible slab feasibility.

My initial idea:
- Tranche A (reserved): covers baseline 120 conc sessions, plus 1.2x buffer (sustained).
- Tranche B (elastic credits): monthly credit pool that can be consumed for bursts; credits redeem for ephemeral GPUs at X tokens-per-credit rate.
- Tranche C (preemptible slab): opportunistic pool for non-critical batch jobs at reduced price; preemptible with 60s eviction notice.

Questions:
1) Can we guarantee 250ms p95 during 8x short spikes if we allocate a 2–3x ephemeral headroom pool?
2) What's a conservative credit-to-gpu conversion for 7B at 512 tokens?
3) Eviction policy: prefer preemptible slab -> elastic credits -> reserved; but critical pinned requests should be protected via weights.

Please reply with numbers/assumptions. I'll consolidate and send to Asha.

Thanks,
Karthik

Karthik / all,

Quick ops numbers (conservative):
- polaris-7B-finetune @ 512 tokens ~= 18 token-ms per token on an A100-like serving kernel under our quant path. For planning, assume ~12K tokens/s per GPU at the observed latency target for interactive (this maps to ~20–25 concurrent low-latency sessions per GPU during sustained use).
- To hit <250ms p95 at 8x spike: baseline reserve + a 2.5x ephemeral headroom across the cluster should cover 95% of 5–20m spikes if we allocate continuous KV-cache warmup for hot prefixes. In practice: baseline of 6 GPUs (covers 120 sessions at 20 sessions/GPU) -> add 9 GPU headroom (ephemeral) for spike windows.
- Credit conversion (rough): 1 GPU-hour equivalent ~= 36,000 credits (assuming 10k tokens/minute baseline conversion used in pricing models). We'll create a cleaner worksheet.

Eviction/priority:
- Weighted eviction with pinned app weights: Polaris can mark up to 15% of sessions as "pinned-critical"; pinned are last to evict.
- Preemptible slab: cheapest but will be terminated first with 60s notice; good for background fine-tuning or batch jobs.

I'll attach a quick tranche matrix (numbers are preliminary).

Ben
Senior Infrastructure PM, Redwood Inference

Subject: Redwood proposal: tranche tiers + soft-eviction policy (Polaris Bio)

Hi Asha / Evan,

Thanks for the thorough requirements. Attached is a concise proposal and the calculation workbook. Summary below — please review and we'll set a short call to lock numbers.

Executive summary (short):
- Baseline (Tranche A, reserved): 6 GPUs (covers 120 concurrent sessions at 20 sessions/GPU sustained). Monthly reserved commitment.
- Elastic credits (Tranche B): equivalent of 180 GPU-hours/month (redeemable for ephemeral GPUs used during burst windows). Designed to cover ~60–80 x 5–20m spikes per month at the profile you provided. Credits roll over up to 15% month-to-month.
- Preemptible slab (Tranche C): optional additional 8 GPU preemptible pool for low-cost background jobs; 60s eviction notice.

Eviction & priority (soft-eviction policy):
1) Priority markers: Polaris may mark sessions as "pinned-critical" (up to 15% of sessions). Pinned-critical are excluded from preemptible eviction and are last to be reclaimed from elastic credits.
2) Eviction order: preemptible slab -> elastic-credit ephemeral -> reserved (only under extreme manual override).
3) Grace window & KV-warm: ephemeral allocations during a spike will respect a 90s soft-grace period for in-flight requests; we keep the KV cache warm for hot prefixes identified in a shared prefix list.
4) Notification & observability: webhook triggers, token-level burn-rate dashboard, and detailed monthly credit consumption report for procurement.

Assumptions: 7B model, 512 token average, A100-like instance perf (see attached workbook for token->GPU-hour conversions). We propose a 30-day trial of the elastic credits at 50% prepaid price to validate real traffic patterns and then finalize a yearly tranche.

Attachments: polaris_tranche_matrix_v1.xlsx, soft_eviction_policy_draft.pdf, SLA-tiered-pricing-09026.xlsx

- Suggested 30-minute call Friday to confirm pinned-session process and instrumentation around hot-prefix lists.
